doc_summary: A project-ideas post from Owain Evans and Stuart Armstrong listing AI safety research projects for collaborators; Evans's own section is a brief call for work on aligning large language models. The document contains little on evaluation realism, so most items are weakly relevant inferences from the stated methods and interests.

items.claim: Prefers testing alignment properties (accuracy, reliability, helpfulness, transparency) on real, contemporary language models over purely abstract treatment, because current LLMs are the concrete systems whose relation to AGI needs to be understood.
items.quote: Aligning large language models with human preferences and other normative criteria. For example, how to make models more accurate, reliable, helpful and transparent.

items.claim: Interested in how far the current LLM paradigm extends toward AGI and what its limits are, framing empirical LLM work as evidence about future systems.
items.quote: How do current language models relate to AGI? What are the limits of the current paradigm?

items.claim: Prefers programmatic experiments with controlled toy agents (grid-worlds with known preferences and biases) over purely philosophical argument, because ground-truth knowledge of the agent's preferences lets one measure how many assumptions are needed (Armstrong's project, shared in the post).
items.quote: The basic idea is to create models of agents in grid-world situations, agents with preferences and biases, and train a classifier to deduce their preferences, given various collections of true assumptions about the agents.

items.claim: Treats evidence of research competence as concrete artifacts (papers, blog posts, courses, reference letters) rather than formal credentials, a preference for demonstrable output over credentials.
items.quote: Research experience in any area of machine learning or a related field. Evidence for this is an academic paper or a blogpost

items.claim: Expects projects to yield tangible, reusable outputs (papers plus example agents or code others can build on) rather than only conceptual claims.
items.quote: The outputs of the project should be a computer science paper and some programmed example agents that others could build on.

items.claim: Concerned with how capabilities or knowledge given to an AI for alignment can raise its power faster than its alignment, so safety interventions must be tested for side effects.
items.quote: knowledge that might increase its power faster than its alignment.

items.claim: Prefers worked examples of agents behaving and misbehaving in varied circumstances alongside analysis, because concrete cases make abstract value-learning risks demonstrable.
items.quote: some examples of agents learning and (mis)behaving in various circumstances.

items.claim: Leaves specific LLM alignment projects open and negotiable with collaborators, signaling flexibility in choosing what to test within broad areas.
items.quote: I have some specific projects in mind that I will discuss with applicants. I’m also open to considering projects proposed by applicants in these general areas.
